subject: RFI: Nimbus Bank - Network Fencing & Threat Assessment
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@nimbusbank.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@nimbusbank.com, procure@nimbusbank.com
Date: 2027-05-22T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: RFI - Network isolation, segmentation and threat assessment for Redwood Inference

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — Nimbus is progressing through our vendor checklist and we need a concise response to a few technical items focused on network fencing and attacker surface containment. Security wants a short threat-summary and a network diagram that shows:
- How tenant traffic is separated (logical and physical boundaries)
- Egress controls for inference requests and logs
- Failure modes that could allow cross-tenant access and controls in place to mitigate them

Can you provide a 1–2 page narrative plus a network diagram and a table of evidence (configs / audit trails)? Procurement would like the materials by EOD Monday May 24 so we can include them in the vendor packet.

Regards,
Alice Chen
Senior Security Engineer, Nimbus Bank
alice.chen@nimbusbank.com
+1-415-555-0123

--
Attachment: nimbus_rfi_template.docx (referenced)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@nimbusbank.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Procure <procure@nimbusbank.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI - Network isolation, segmentation and threat assessment for Redwood Inference

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask. We can deliver a concise packet addressing the three items you listed. High-level plan:

1) Narrative (2 pages) summarizing our isolation model, routing and egress controls;
2) Annotated network diagram showing control plane, serving plane, tenant VPCs, and egress chokepoints;
3) Evidence table: SOC2 excerpts, sample VPC flow logs, KMS key rotation audit snippet, recent patching cadence report.

Well attach the PDF diagram and an XLS with the mapped evidence. Quick notes up front:
- Tenants are logically isolated by per-tenant namespaces and by network-level security groups; Dedicated customers can be placed in isolated GPU pools (no shared hosts).
- The control plane is SaaS-managed and never processes customer inference payloads in plaintext when customers opt for Private deployment; for hosted inference we provide customer-managed KMS options and per-tenant encryption-at-rest.
- Egress is allowed only through a set of managed NAT gateways with egress filtering and DLP hooks where required; logs are retained per contract for audit.

Were drafting the packet now and will send the attachments by end of day Monday (May 24). If you need a quick live walk-through before then, I can do a 30-minute call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
+1-617-555-2077

--
Attachment: planned: redwood_nimbus_network_fencing_diagram.pdf, redwood_kms_and_keys_matrix.xlsx

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI - internal: Nimbus packet draft + quick clarifications

Karthik / team — Ive attached the draft diagram and evidence map in the shared drive link (internal only). A couple of internal clarifications to call out in the narrative so we don't overclaim:

- Isolation: Hosted customers share a multi-tenant serving plane by default; isolation relies on process-level tenant namespaces, KV cache scoping and network ACLs. Dedicated customers have separate GPU pools and can get isolated subnets.
- Cross-tenant failure modes: the largest residual risk is side-channel leakage via shared GPU caches for hosted multi-tenant serving. Mitigations: quantization-aware cache partitioning, periodic cache flush on model rollover, and model pinning options to avoid co-tenancy. Note we provide recommendations on request to move high-sensitivity models to Dedicated or Private.
- Egress: We need to note we support customer-managed egress (VPC peering / PrivateLink) for Private deployments — mention this as a hard-control option.

Ive suggested language in the draft (see bullet comments). Hannah, can you confirm the KMS audit snippet we intend to include is the May rotation log (key-redwood-prod-2027-05)?

Rishi
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@nimbusbank.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@nimbusbank.com, security@nimbusbank.com
Date: 2027-05-24T07:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI - Network isolation, segmentation and threat assessment for Redwood Inference

Karthik — this is great; quick clarifications before you send the final packet:

1) For the side-channel risk note, can you provide brief wording on how Redwood detects anomalous KV/cache usage patterns and what telemetry is available to customers?
2) For egress controls, can you confirm whether the NAT gateways support explicit allowlists by outbound FQDNs and whether logs include hostname-level resolution?
3) Finally, procurement asked whether you can provide an example SLA exception process if Nimbus requests a dedicated capacity carveout with accelerated provisioning (we may need this for a pilot).

Can you include those three points in the packet? If its easier, a 20-minute call today would also work — I have 11:30–12:30 PT free.

Thanks,
Alice

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@nimbusbank.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, procure@nimbusbank.com
Date: 2027-05-24T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI - Network isolation, segmentation and threat assessment for Redwood Inference

Alice — attached is the final packet per your checklist. Short answers to the clarifications embedded up front:

1) Side-channel detection telemetry: Redwood exposes per-namespace metrics for KV cache hit/miss rates, per-model token latency distributions, and anomalous process CPU/GPU usage alerts via our Console. Customers can push these metrics to their SIEM via our Prometheus-compatible endpoints and we include example alert rules in the evidence XLS. Weve also added recommended thresholds and a short runbook for investigating bursty cache access patterns.

2) Egress allowlists and hostname logging: Our managed NAT gateways support outbound FQDN allowlists and integration with DNS logging. Logs include resolved hostnames when DNS resolution happens through our resolvers; we call this out as an optional Private deployment feature (customer-managed VPCs will use customer DNS and logging).

3) SLA exception for dedicated provisioning: We included a procurement-ready workflow (Doc ID in Drive) that outlines accelerated provisioning steps, expected timelines, and required pre-commitments. For pilot carveouts we can guarantee a provisioning SLA of 7 business days given a confirmed capacity commit and signed SOW; permanent capacity follows the standard Dedicated onboarding timelines.

Attachments in packet: redwood_nimbus_network_fencing_diagram.pdf (annotated), redwood_kms_and_keys_matrix.xlsx (evidence map), runbook_cache_anomaly_response.md (excerpt).

Let us know if you want a short walkthrough; happy to join the call at 11:30 PT.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
--
Attachment stubs: redwood_nimbus_network_fencing_diagram.pdf (3 pages, annotated), redwood_kms_and_keys_matrix.xlsx (5 sheets), runbook_cache_anomaly_response.md (1 page excerpt)
